summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 17 and 18 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022, seeking condonation of delay in complying with the procedure of issuance of Renewable Energy Certificates for FY 2023-24 and other consequential reliefs. 3. The Petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 17 and 18 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022 (REC Regulations, 2022) for seeking condonation of delay in complying with the procedure of issuance of Renewable Energy Certificates (REC) for FY 2023-24 and other consequential reliefs. - (b) _Direct NLDC to issue Renewable Energy Certificates for FY 2023-24 in favour of the Petitioner;_ - (c) _Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice._ - (b) The Petitioner was unable to approach the NLDC for issuance of RECs within the period of three months from the end of the financial year as stipulated under Regulation 10(3) of the REC Regulations 2022. Due to various reasons beyond the control of the Petitioner, substantial time was consumed in completing the aforesaid steps, as elaborated below: - (d) The Petitioner complied with all requirements under the REC Regulations 2022 and obtained all approvals and recommendations certifying its eligibility and entitlement to the RECS for FY 2023-24. - (e) Therefore, the Petitioner requests the Commission to exercise its power to relax under Regulation 18 of the REC Regulations, 2022, to (i) condone the delay of eight-two (82) days in approaching NLDC; and (ii) direct NLDC to issue RECs in favour of the Petitioner for FY 2023-24. 2. During the course of the hearing, no one was present on behalf of the Petitioner. However, considering the nature of the dispute involved in the Petition, the Commission admitted the Petition and issued notice to the Respondent. The Commission also directed the Respondent to file its reply and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any. 3. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition was filed seeking condonation of the delay of 82 days in approaching the NLDC for issuance of RECs for FY 2023-24, in terms of the REC Regulations, 2022. The counsel for the Petitioner also submitted that under Regulation 10(3), the application for issuance of RECs was required to be filed within three months of the end of the financial year; however, due to reasons beyond the Petitioner's control, the prescribed timeline could not be adhered to. It was also submitted that the Commission condoned similar delay in its several orders. The Counsel further pointed out that despite the lapse of considerable time, the Respondent, NLDC, did not file any reply in the matter. Considering the submissions of the counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission granted another opportunity to the Respondent to file its reply, if any and the Petitioner, to file its rejoinder. 4. Due to a paucity of time, the matter could not be taken for the hearing and was accordingly adjourned. 5. During the course of the hearing, the counsel of the Respondent, NLDC, submitted that the Respondent did not wish to file any reply in the matter, and the Commission may consider the prayers of the Petitioner as may be deemed fit. Further, on the request of the counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its note of submissions. Subject to the above, the Commission reserved the matter for order. 6. Accordingly, on 14.02.2026, the Petitioner submitted the short note of the submissions. 7. The Commission has heard the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondent and has carefully perused the records. 10. From the above, we observe that the Petitioner was required to approach the Respondent, NLDC, within three months from the end of the financial year, along with the received certification from APERC. We observe that the Petitioner could not adhere to the timeline and has applied for issuance of RECs for FY 2023-24 with a delay of 82 days. As submitted by the Petitioner, the delay was due to various factors, primarily related to the collection and collation of renewable energy procurement data and compliance with the requisite regulatory and procedural requirements. Further, during the hearing, the Respondent, NLDC, submitted that the Commission may consider the Petitioner's prayers as it deems fit. _The Commission may, from time to time, issue such practice directions and orders as considered appropriate for the implementation of these regulations_ _The Commission may by general or special order, for reasons to be recorded in writing, and after giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties likely to be affected, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by interested person(s)._ 13. In our view, the delay in the application for issuance of the REC is procedural in nature due to the reasons stated by the Petitioner and is not likely to prejudice any of the stakeholders, including the Respondent. Accordingly, the timelines stipulated under Regulation 10(3) of the REC Regulations 2022 are hereby relaxed, and the Petitioner is permitted to file its application for the issuance of RECs before the Central Agency for FY 2023-24. 14. Further, the Respondent NLDC is directed to issue the RECs for FY 2023-24 to the Petitioner, APCPDCL, after due verification and satisfying itself that the Petitioner meets all other conditions and has submitted all the required documents for the issuance of RECs.
title: Petition under Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 17 and 18 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022, seeking condonation of delay in complying with the procedure of issuance of Renewable Energy Certificates for FY 2023-24 and other consequential reliefs. Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Company Limited
